lead.headline: Magnitude 7.4 quake kills 132 across western Colombia
lead.dek: President Abelardo de la Espriella, sworn in three days earlier, declared a state of emergency; Cali imposed a curfew.
body: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake killed at least 132 people and injured 570 in western Colombia on Monday, the strongest to strike the country this century, with rescue crews still searching collapsed buildings in Cali and Pereira.

The quake struck near San Jose del Palmar, in Choco department about 250 miles west of Bogota, shortly after 7:30 a.m. Monday, and at least 21 aftershocks followed within hours. NBC News reported three hospitals collapsed and roughly 5,000 homes damaged.

briefs.headline: Trump orders fewer recommended childhood vaccines
briefs.summary: RSV and hepatitis A and B move to high-risk children only, MMR splits into three doses, and HHS has 90 days to reassess timing.

briefs.headline: July was the hottest month on record in the Lower 48
briefs.summary: NOAA put the contiguous U.S. average at 76.89F, 0.125F above the July 1936 record set in the Dust Bowl.

briefs.headline: Minnesota and Wisconsin vote in test of the left
briefs.summary: Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan meets Rep. Angie Craig in Minnesota's Senate primary; state Rep. Francesca Hong leads Wisconsin's Democratic field for governor.

briefs.headline: Syrian court sentences Assad to death in absentia
briefs.summary: Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher were convicted over the 14-year war; cousin Atef Najib, tried in person, drew the same sentence.

briefs.headline: Trump demands Iran pay for 50 years of damage
briefs.summary: He met Tehran's reparations condition for reopening the Strait of Hormuz with a counterclaim covering the USS Cole and other deaths.

briefs.headline: Zelenskyy says North Korean missiles hit Zaporizhzhia
briefs.summary: Six died and 19 were wounded there in overnight strikes that also hit Kyiv and Dnipropetrovsk region, where three more died.

briefs.headline: Drug policy director reports 41.6% drop in overdose deaths
briefs.summary: Dr. Stephen Loyd told the Joint Standing Committee on Health the drop is measured from pre-pandemic levels and that rates remain 2.5 times the national average.

briefs.headline: Lawmakers say child death report left out required detail
briefs.summary: The review team reported 29 child deaths from January through April in three bullet points. Del. Kayla Young said lawmakers mandated more.

regional.item: Council introduced ordinances setting data rules and misuse penalties before any Flock contract is signed.
Monday's storms cut power to more than 2,000 Appalachian Power customers, the most of any county.

fishing.line: 90 cfs and rising, gauge at 1.58 ft - prime wading water.
Sound highs 7:23 a.m. and 8:01 p.m.; water 78.1F at Wrightsville Beach, 25 miles down the coast.

briefs.headline: Teddy Bridgewater retires again at 33 after 11 seasons
briefs.summary: Detroit placed him on the reserve/retired list Sunday and signed Josh Dobbs to a one-year, $1.425 million deal.

briefs.headline: WVU rebuilds a defense that ranked 112th in scoring
briefs.summary: The Mountaineers allowed 30.8 points a game last season, 36.2 in Big 12 play; senior linebacker Ben Cutter is the only returning top-17 tackler.

briefs.headline: Total eclipse crosses Spain on Wednesday, first since 1912
briefs.summary: The Moon's shadow enters Galicia about 19:27 and leaves the Balearics about 20:35; totality lasts under 1 minute 48 seconds.

briefs.headline: Saturn's magnetic funnel sits in the afternoon, not at noon
briefs.summary: Cassini data from 2004 to 2010 put the cusp between 13:00 and 15:00 local time, dragged by the planet's 10.7-hour spin.

weather_ear: The forecast follows at 7:15, from Jim Claudtore.
kicker: Sumo sat out; there was nothing between tournaments.
